arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Stewart argued the Court must distinguish between two types of confusion.
Mr. Dvoretzky argued the FDA ignored the risk because it disliked Merck's phrasing.
Mr. Frederick argued brand-name drug makers must keep labels up to date at all times.
Justice Gorsuch asked about the period after the March 2010 letter when the FDA launched an investigation.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between federal drug regulation and state tort law. It determines whether patients can sue drug makers for inadequate warnings when the FDA rejects proposed label changes. The outcome shapes the balance between federal oversight and state consumer protection.
